rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A transformer changes AC voltage based on mutual induction. It uses the turns ratio to step voltage up or down, while ideally conserving power. Energy losses are mitigated through core design and winding techniques.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Transformer Ratio V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p
Power relation V_p I_p = V_s I_s (for ideal)
Efficiency η = (P_out / P_in) × 100%

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Assuming transformer works on DC ✅ Transformer only operates on AC as it requires a *changing* magnetic flux to induce EMF (DC has constant flux).  ·  ❌ Thinking voltage ratio is independent of current ratio ✅ According to the law of conservation of energy (P_in = P_out for an ideal transformer), voltage and current are inversely proportional: V_p/V_s = I_s/I_p.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Note 1: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. If N_s > N_p, it is a step-up transformer.  ·  Note 2: Transformers operate only on AC.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Transformer:** An electrical device based on mutual induction that changes the voltage level of an AC supply.  ·  It works on the principle of electromagnetic induction: a varying current in the primary coil induces an EMF in the secondary coil via a common magnetic core.  ·  Transformers can be step-up (increase voltage) or step-down (decrease voltage).
